subject: QBR: trajectory and sprint fallout triage (product & eng)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: trajectory and sprint fallout triage (product & eng)

Team —

Ahead of next week’s QBR I wanted to surface the current state of the product roadmap and where the delivery risks are concentrated. I’m keeping this concise so the pack can call out the right mitigations. Summary below.

Current trajectory (next 6 weeks)
- Gen-Cache v2 (priority platform feature): ETA currently 4/12, high impact on latency/cost targets if delayed.
- Reranker A/B: small feature flag rollout planned 3/29; dependent on infra perf metrics for 2k qps.
- Embedding v3: scheduled 4/5, lower risk but requires quantization pick for memory limits.

Top delivery risks (ranked)
1) Gen-Cache v2: unresolved kernel fallback for mixed-precision builds (owner: infra-eng). Likelihood: medium-high. Mitigation: backfill fallback path + canary on dedicated pool.
2) Scaling for Reranker: autoscaler tuning still under experiment; if we miss, can’t support planned A/B throughput for AtlasHealth pilot. Likelihood: medium.
3) Embedding memory regression after quantization: small chance but high customer impact for long sequences.

Asks (concrete):
- Vivek: need decision on risk appetite for Gen-Cache canary vs. delaying GA by 1 sprint.
- Laura: please produce a one-page risks slide we can slot in the QBR deck, with owners and timelines.
- Monica: confirm customer-level mitigation asks for AtlasHealth (Sam Turner) and whether we should pre-announce a targeted window.

I’ve attached a short snapshot (see related Drive link) and flagged the highest-priority Jira tickets. Reply with the owner-level commitments and any change to ETA by 11am PT.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR_Roadmap_Summary.pdf (snapshot)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: trajectory and sprint fallout triage (product & eng)

Ben —

Thanks for the concise callout. A few directives from my side so we can close this before the pack deadline:

1) Gen-Cache v2: Do not GA until we validate fallback on the quantized pipelines. Action: infra-eng to deliver fallback by 2028-03-28. If that slips, schedule a controlled canary (limited customers, dedicated pool) on 4/03. We should codify rollback steps (time to revert, token limits).

2) Reranker autoscaling: product and infra must pair on a weekend load test and an autoscaler tuning run (owners: Monica + infra-eng). Schedule: 3/24 weekend run; report 3/26.

3) Embedding v3: engineering to validate 95th percentile memory under 32GB GPU; provide run artifacts by 3/30.

Laura — please work with Ben to produce the one-pager with clear owner columns and customer impact. Monica — loop in AtlasHealth (Sam) privately to set expectation that we may throttle the reranker in the pilot window if autoscaler misses.

CC’ing Monica and Laura here to capture next steps. I’m asking Engineering Managers to be ready for a 4pm sync if we need immediate trade decisions.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
CEO (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Sam Turner <sam.turner@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: trajectory and sprint fallout triage (product & eng)

Ben / Vivek —

Adding customer context for AtlasHealth (Sam included). Their pilot traffic profile spikes during morning syncs (06:00–09:00 PT) and the reranker is a critical gating factor. If we can’t hit the autoscale window they’ve asked about, they will pause the A/B and that materially changes our QBR metric narrative.

Proposed operational mitigation (short):
- Move their pilot to a dedicated burst pool for first 2 weeks of A/B (minimal code changes, infra config only). Owner: Partnerships + Infra (partners@cloudops.io can provision).
- If Gen-Cache fallback is delayed, throttle long sequences for AtlasHealth only (feature-flagged per-customer).

I’ve attached the QBR snapshot that includes the customer-facing language we can use.

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR_Roadmap_Summary.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR: trajectory and sprint fallout triage (product & eng)

Team —

Attached is the consolidated triage & runbook table. Highlights:
- Owners and timelines aligned (see action owner column).
- Risk severity mapping (P0/P1/P2). Gen-Cache is elevated to P0 until fallback is validated.
- Canary plan for Gen-Cache: deploy to dedicated pool 4/03, observe token-level latency and error rate for 48 hours. Rollback plan is a single config flip (track SUP-5423).
- Autoscale weekend run scheduled 3/24; Monica to confirm CloudOps provisioning by EOD 3/23.

Please review the runbook table and confirm the owner commits in-line in the doc. If there are no objections I will slot the one-pager into the QBR deck this afternoon.

Laura Bennett
VP, Program Management
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-delta-issuetable.xlsx

All — thanks for the quick turn. I reviewed the runbook and the QBR snapshot; approve slotting the one-pager into the deck.

Next steps I’ll own:
- Confirm canary gating checklist is complete by 3/30.
- Update the QBR slide to reflect the dedicated-pool mitigation for AtlasHealth.

If any owner cannot meet their committed date, flag me immediately.

Ben
summary: Leadership thread coordinating QBR content: Ben surfaces roadmap delivery risks; Vivek issues directives; Monica adds customer mitigation and CloudOps provisioning; Laura consolidates runbook and attachments with owners and timelines; Ben approves inclusion in QBR and lists next steps.
